title: Aliasing Mutable Parameters with Globals
pattern: A function accepts a mutable reference/pointer parameter while also directly modifying a global variable, where the caller might pass a reference to that very same global variable.
why_bad: This creates a severe "aliasing" bug. If the mutable parameter is an alias for the global variable, updates to one will silently overwrite the other in non-obvious, chaotic ways. It destroys equational reasoning and lexical isolation.
detection: A function reads/writes a global/static mutable variable `G` while simultaneously taking a mutable parameter `P`, without proving that `P` and `G` reside at distinct memory locations. (In safe Rust, this is prevented at compile-time, but is common in `unsafe` blocks or in C++).
source: *Code Complete* by Steve McConnell (Chapter 13, "Bizarre and exciting aliasing problems with global data"); *Types and Programming Languages* by Benjamin C. Pierce (Chapter 13, "References", "Aliasing").
